full_judgment: 2. Heard the learned Advocates Perused the petition, the counter-affidavits and the affidavit-in-reply on record. Mr. Abdul Huq in his counter-affidavit has stated that in May, 1969 he went to Chuadanga to see his ailing sister where Mr. Ayub Ali a senior Advocate of the local Bar along with an old man met him and on their request he agreed to file the second appeal. It was further stated in the counter-affidavit that the learned Advocate did not know any of the appellants excepting the old man whose name also he did not remember and that the balance of the agreed amount of Taka 201/- was never paid to him. It has been further stated by Mr. Abdul Huq that in January, 1971, appellant No. 1 informed him over trunk telephone that the decree has already been executed and possession of the suit land has been taken through the court after evicting the appellants and accordingly he was instructed not to proceed with the appeal. When the matter came up for hearing under Order 41, Rule 11 C.P.C. the craned Advocate made the submission as aforesaid and the appeal was dismissed for non-prosecution.
